newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Nov 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Nov 6.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- New Aspiration Party (NAP) makes big money promises in bid to romance teachers. Despite complaints that they have improperly tried to enlist the help of teachers in their campaign, NAP members yesterday stepped up their efforts to win support from one of the country's biggest professions.

Several seniors NAP members yesrerday attended rallies aimed at teachers thoughout the country and vowed to improve the quality of teachers's lives if the party leads the next government. (THE NATION)

- Prosecutor drops land reform charges. Charges against 67 people in the Phuket land reform affair, including Democrat Party leader Chuan Leekpai and members of his former cabinet, were dropped by the Office of the Supreme Attorney General yesterday.
The dismissal of the 17 cases will help the Democrats put the mistakes behind them and deprive their politicians of ammunition in the run-up to the general election.

- U.S. President Bill Clinton announced the return of tax privileges under the generalised system of preferences (GSP) to Thailand for various exports to the U.S., according to the Foreign Trade Department.

The privilages had been removed on Jan 1. The return of the previlages was effective as of October 1. Exports which will benefit include dry guarva; mango and mangosteen; dry tamarind; processed crab meat; uncooked pasta; flavoured corn; pineapple jam; lychee and longan; tanned hides; and acrylic polyester fibre buttons. (THE NATION)
- Board fails in quest to delay tariff cuts. The finance Minister has rejected a Board of Investment bid for it to delay import tariff cuts by at least one year.

The scheme had been planned for the last four years, and industries affected had enough time to adjust to the charages, Caretaker Finance Minister Chaiyawat Vibulsawasdi said yesterday. (BANGKOK POST)
